files.Title: BOOSE.AboutBOOSE
files.Summary: Basic Object Orientated Software Engineering. This is a set of classes for implementing the BOOSE language. It is currently private, so you will not be able to extend the classes, only examine the documentation and use the public interfaces. To replace class functionality you can either implement the relevant interface to completely replace all functionality, or extend the relevant class (if the library is made public) and override the interface methods, which will allow the calling of base methods in the original class. Example of adding a command to BOOSE. Here I will call the new program AppBOOSE and append App to class names (but you can call them what you like). step 1 extend ICanvas to have your new draw command that will be called when its command is executed, IAppCanvas. step 2 extend this new interface with a class (AppCanvas) which creates a drawing object (bitmap?) does all the actual drawing. step 3 extend appropriate command Interface to create a new command class. i.e. Rect(width, height) would extend ICommandTwoParameters. step 4 extend the original factory if you want to use any of its existing commands (by calling base.MakeCommand() after looking for your new commands) or ICommandFactory if completely replacing it. BOOSE is restricted via a set of constants that limit its functionality unless the restrictions are turned off. They can only be turned off at the source code level (i.e. by the author only). Restrictions are persistant through multiple runs (i.e. if you have a program that defines two variables and run it three times it will have defined six variables and will trigger the restrictions. 1.04 reduced restrictions on graphics commands. 1.06 added restrictions method in evaluation, to move where restrictions are located. 1.08 added new restrctions to Array, moved restrictions from evaluation to Int, Real and Boolean. 1.09 added new restrictions to compound commands and methods, made program size simpler. 1.1 fixed bug stopping restrictions on arrays. 1.2 increased number of execution cycles in StoredProgram from 50 to 200. 2.0 Complier conditionals to implemenmt restrictions.

files.Title: BOOSE.Boolean
files.Summary: Boolean datatype, also used for Conditional Commands.

files.Title: BOOSE.Call
files.Summary:
Command to call a previously defined method.

method int testMethod int one, int two testMethod = one* two end method int global = 55 call testMethod 10 15

files.Title: BOOSE.Canvas
files.Summary: Abstract class that implements CanvasInterface. See CanvasInterface documentation for what to implement. This class handles all the drawing on your system according to above documentation. BOOSE does not by default specify a default drawing Canvas (only this).

files.Title: BOOSE.CanvasCommand
files.Summary: Abstract class that is inherited by derived canvas commands that draw on a canvas. It stores the x and y positions of the last drawing operation.

files.Title: BOOSE.CanvasException
files.Summary: Exception that should be thrown by operations that fail on the Canvas.

files.Title: BOOSE.Cast
files.Summary:
Cast real values to int values. Syntax: cast intVar realVar Both variables must be previously defined.

real circ = 100.123\nint c\ncast c circ\ncircle c

files.Title: BOOSE.Circle
files.Summary:
Draw a circle round the current cursor position.

circle 50 Canvas exception if a non-integer is passed.

files.Title: BOOSE.Command
files.Summary: Abstract class for BOOSE commands. Can handle a parameter list or expression. This class will seperate the parameters or expression from the command and store in the "ParameterList". The Command's Compile() method is called by the parser and this is expected to set the Command's parameters. BOOSE implementation of commands makes definitions "sealed". Sealed classes cannot be inherited, so you can't use what's there to remove the restrictions, you will have to totally rewrite them.

files.Title: BOOSE.CommandException
files.Summary: Exception genereted by the StoredProgram class when a command fails. This represents a run-time error. Any StoredProgram class should catch such an exception and report the problem to the user.

files.Title: BOOSE.CommandOneParameter
files.Summary: Commands with one parameter. The command system adds one parameter at a time. Can be used by any one parameter command.

files.Title: BOOSE.CommandThreeParameters
files.Summary: Commands with two parameters. Each command has an Xpos and Ypos that operates from the current cursor position.

files.Title: BOOSE.CommandTwoParameters
files.Summary: Commands with two parameters. Each command has an Xpos and Ypos that operates from the current cursor position.

files.Title: BOOSE.CompoundCommand
files.Summary: CompoundCommand is a building block for shared functionality between CompoundCommands, such as IF, WHILE, FOR ,ELSE and ENDS Classes the inherit from here tend to be "sealed" so that they cnnot be inherited from to manipulate restrictions.

files.Title: BOOSE.ConditionalCommand.conditionalTypes
files.Summary: Enumerated type to represent individual conditional commands.

files.Title: BOOSE.ConditionalCommand
files.Summary: Used for Ifs, Whiles and Fors

files.Title: BOOSE.DrawTo
files.Summary:
Draw a line from to current cursor position to the provided x,y position.

drawto 200,200

files.Title: BOOSE.Else
files.Summary: An Else is like an Endif but it pops the corresponding If off the stack and pushes itself on so that it becomes the corresponding command to the end

files.Title: BOOSE.End
files.Summary: End command for If/While/For/Method. BOOSE has only one End type command which has a parameter to say what it belongs so eg. "end if". End checks Boose types for the ciorresponding command (If/While/For/Method) and will likely require a complete rewrite to replcae those commands. It would probbaly be easier to replace Parser, StoredProgram, CompoundCommand and this. Look at the metghods each provides, if you like, and try and fill in their fucntionality.

files.Title: BOOSE.Evaluation
files.Summary: An evaluation encompasses all things that can have a value, such as variables, expressions and conditions used in loops and ifs.

files.Title: BOOSE.FactoryException
files.Summary: Exception genereted by the a CommandFactory. It represents a command not being part of BOOSE.

files.Title: BOOSE.For
files.Summary: For command. Adds processing at compile() and execute() to process a for command.

files.Title: BOOSE.ICanvas
files.Summary: Implement ICanvas for your BOOSE renderer. It has an Xpos and Ypos of the current cursor position and a pen colour. Your class should implement the methods below to draw on its "bitmap" (i.e. it may not be a bitmap, it could draw in ASCII text for example).

files.Title: BOOSE.ICommand
files.Summary: Interface for BOOSE commands. Any Command class should implement this interface and be generated by a CommandFactory that implements the ICommandFactory interface. Contains methods to set the Command up after its creation, manage its parameters when it is compiled and execute it when it is called.

files.Title: BOOSE.ICommandFactory
files.Summary: To add commands to BOOSE you must create a CommandFactory that uses this interface. You should extend the existing BOOSE:CommandFactory (which implements this interface) and then implement the MakeCommand() method. It shoudld create a new command object based on the string passed. Any standard BOOSE commands can then be made by calling base.MakeCommand(); If you do not extend the existing CommandFactory you must implement this interface and create a MakeCommand() method that creates all commands, including the standard BOOSE commands.

files.Title: BOOSE.IEvaluation
files.Summary: IEvaluation adds properties to get and set an Evaluations name, value and expression. An evaluation can be a variable declaration, such as "int total" or "real area". It can be change an exprerssion to change the value of a variable, such as "total = total + 1", the part after the "=" is an referred to as an "expression". In the first two cases the parser will generate an Int object and a Real Object. In the third case it will generate a "Evaluation" object. Not currently used in the standard implementation of BOOSE.

files.Title: BOOSE.IParser
files.Summary: The Parser Class takes a BOOSE program as a String with each line seperated by '\n' and creates command objects for each valid command and stores them in the passed in StoredProgram. Exceptions shoulod bee generated for any syntax errors by the comand objects themselves. The parser should catch these exceptions and add them to an error list. When each valid command is generated its Compile() method is called. The valid command will have its parameters processed and any variables identified. It is the role of StoredProgram to run the commands.

files.Title: BOOSE.IStoredProgram
files.Summary: Runtime interface for a StoredProgram. A StoredProgram is a collection of commands that can be executed in order. It has a program counter (PC) that keeps track of the current command being executed. It also has a collection of variables that can be used in expressions. The StoredProgram can be reset, and it can be run until there are no more commands left to execute.

files.Title: BOOSE.If
files.Summary: If command. Adds processing at compile() and execute() to process an if command.

files.Title: BOOSE.Int
files.Summary: Command Class to define and store integer values.

files.Title: BOOSE.Method
files.Summary: Method declaration command. Overcoming method restrictions will require a complete rewrite. It would be simpler to do this after Parser and StoredProgram. You are getting to the stage where you need to do a big rewrite.

files.Title: BOOSE.MoveTo
files.Summary: Set the cursor position, for subsequent drawing operations, to the provide x,y position.

files.Title: BOOSE.Parser
files.Summary: The parser takes a program, who's lines are seperated by "\n", and attempts to create a StoredProgram. Once the SToredProgram has been created it then can be run. As much processing that can be done is done here because it has no run penalty (other than starting the program). Command objects are created and their parameters processed as much as possible. Variables are checked for existance but expressions cannot be processed until runtime.

files.Title: BOOSE.ParserException
files.Summary: Exception genereted by the Parser class to denote syntax errors. ANy systax error should proivide information about what the error is. A Parser shoudl catch these exceptions, append a line number and generate a syntax error list.

files.Title: BOOSE.Peek
files.Summary: Peek an array, i.e. get the value of an array cell. [variable] = peek [array name] [row] [optional column]

files.Title: BOOSE.PenColour
files.Summary: Set the pen for the next drawing operations to the provided r,g,b colour.

files.Title: BOOSE.Poke
files.Summary: Poke an array, i.e. set the value of an array cell. poke [array name] [row] [optional column] = [value]

files.Title: BOOSE.Real
files.Summary: Class for a Real Number Variable.

files.Title: BOOSE.Rect
files.Summary: Draw a rectangle of provided with and heigh with the current cursor position being the top left corner.

files.Title: BOOSE.RestrictionException
files.Summary: Exception thrown when restrictions are breached. If you get this you need to write your own code for the facility. This only occurs when using the library code from a DLL. If you are writing your own classes this exception is irrelevant.

files.Title: BOOSE.StoredProgram
files.Summary: A collection class for storing a program of Command objects, extends ArrayList to add a program counter and a flag to indicate that the syntax is ok and the program valid. Adds methods below to process variables and methods and implements flow of control for ifs and loops.

files.Title: BOOSE.StoredProgramException
files.Summary: Exception genereted by the StoredProgram class. This excption should be thrown by a StoredProgram if an operation like returning the value of a non-existant variable or attempt to call a non-existant method happens.

files.Title: BOOSE.VarException
files.Summary: Exception raised by variable commands.if their expressions cannot be evaluated.

files.Title: BOOSE.While
files.Summary: While command. So far blank as it doesn't do anything beyond ConditionalCommand but it makes the code clearer (in the factory).
